hex.title: Hex
hex.author: Thomas Olde Heuvelt
hex.why: Comments name it as a one-star read.

children of ruin.title: Children of Ruin
children of ruin.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
children of ruin.why: Second Children of Time book, following strange non-human life forms; readers enjoy its alien biology.

one second after.title: One second after
one second after.author: William R. Forstchen
one second after.why: An EMP attack shuts down America and a man protects his family; a top pick for readers of apocalypse fiction.

deacon king kong.title: Deacon King Kong
deacon king kong.author: James McBride
deacon king kong.why: An old church deacon shoots a drug dealer in 1969 Brooklyn and the neighbourhood reacts; funny and warm.

let the right one in.title: Let the right one in
let the right one in.author: John Ajvide Lindqvist
let the right one in.why: A bullied boy befriends a strange girl in a Swedish suburb; a chilling vampire novel.

east of eden by john steinbeck.title: East of Eden
east of eden by john steinbeck.author: John Steinbeck
east of eden by john steinbeck.why: Two California families reenact Cain and Abel across generations; many readers call it phenomenal.

screwtape letters.title: The Screwtape Letters
screwtape letters.author: C. S. Lewis
screwtape letters.why: A senior demon coaches his nephew on tempting a man; witty Christian reflections on morality.

paradise.title: Paradise
paradise.author: Toni Morrison
paradise.why: Comments do not discuss this specific book.

on tyranny.title: On Tyranny
on tyranny.author: Timothy Snyder
on tyranny.why: Twenty short lessons from history on resisting authoritarianism; a quick read.

leech.title: Leech
leech.author: Hiron Ennes
leech.why: A doctor arrives in a frozen medieval-style land with a strange parasite; brilliant body horror with mind games.

killers of a certain age.title: Killers of a Certain Age
killers of a certain age.author: Deanna Raybourn
killers of a certain age.why: Comments do not clearly recommend it.

incandescent.title: The Incandescent
incandescent.author: Emily Tesh
incandescent.why: A teacher at a magical school faces a dark threat; readers call it absolutely brilliant.

pattern recognition.title: Pattern Recognition
pattern recognition.author: William Gibson
pattern recognition.why: A brand consultant tracks the maker of mysterious online footage; readers say it deserves the hype of Neuromancer.

word for world is forest.title: The Word for World Is Forest
word for world is forest.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
word for world is forest.why: Humans colonise a forest world and its people resist; Le Guin's explicit commentary on the Vietnam war.

wide wide sea.title: The Wide Wide Sea
wide wide sea.author: Hampton Sides
wide wide sea.why: The final voyage of Captain Cook, beautifully told by Sides.

flatland.title: Flatland
flatland.author: Edwin Abbott Abbott
flatland.why: A square explores dimensions in a Victorian satire; loved for its formatting and ideas.

onyx storm.title: Onyx Storm
onyx storm.author: Rebecca Yarros
onyx storm.why: Comments are mixed, one reader could not get into it.

evicted.title: Evicted
evicted.author: Matthew Desmond
evicted.why: Follows eight families facing eviction and housing insecurity; eye-opening social research.

dragon rider.title: Dragon Rider
dragon rider.author: Cornelia Funke
dragon rider.why: A young dragon and his friends search for a hidden valley; a children's favourite.

absolution.title: Absolution
absolution.author: Jeff VanderMeer
absolution.why: Comments are mixed and partly about other books.

vorrh.title: The Vorrh
vorrh.author: Brian Catling
vorrh.why: A haunted forest in a surreal alternate world; beautifully written and opaque, making readers ask what they are reading.

nothing.title: Nothing
nothing.author: Janne Teller
nothing.why: Teenagers try to prove meaning exists by sacrificing things; unsettling and philosophical.

sea of rust.title: Sea of Rust
sea of rust.author: C. Robert Cargill
sea of rust.why: Robots in a post-human world struggle to survive; readers like it for its AI characters.

people of the book.title: People of the Book
people of the book.author: Geraldine Brooks
people of the book.why: A conservator traces the history of a rare Hebrew manuscript across centuries; readers enjoyed it.

ill be gone in the dark.title: I'll Be Gone in the Dark
ill be gone in the dark.author: Michelle McNamara
ill be gone in the dark.why: A writer's obsessive hunt for the Golden State Killer, completed after her death; chilling and absorbing.

leviathan.title: Leviathan
leviathan.author: Scott Westerfeld
leviathan.why: Alternate-WWI steampunk adventure with fabricated beasts and walkers; a series readers reread.

collected schizophrenias.title: The Collected Schizophrenias
collected schizophrenias.author: Esmé Weijun Wang
collected schizophrenias.why: Personal essays about living with schizoaffective disorder, sharp and honest.

tortilla flat.title: Tortilla Flat
tortilla flat.author: John Steinbeck
tortilla flat.why: A group of friends in Monterey enjoy a ramshackle life; a funny, warm Steinbeck favourite.

binti.title: Binti
binti.author: Nnedi Okorafor
binti.why: Comments call it among the worst books they've read.

half his age.title: Half His Age
half his age.author: Jennette McCurdy
half his age.why: Comments only mention reading it without recommendation.

prestige.title: The Prestige
prestige.author: Christopher Priest
prestige.why: Two rival Victorian magicians feud and sabotage each other; twisty, better than the film according to readers.

last chance to see.title: Last Chance to See
last chance to see.author: Douglas Adams and Mark Carwardine
last chance to see.why: Adams and a zoologist travel the world to find endangered animals; a fun, witty book.

riyria revelations.title: Riyria Revelations
riyria revelations.author: Michael J. Sullivan
riyria revelations.why: Two thieves become entangled in a kingdom's secrets in this fun, fast fantasy series.

invention of morel.title: The Invention of Morel
invention of morel.author: Adolfo Bioy Casares
invention of morel.why: A fugitive on an island sees mysterious people who may not be real; praised by Borges as nearly perfect.

frankenstein by mary shelley.title: Frankenstein
frankenstein by mary shelley.author: Mary Shelley
frankenstein by mary shelley.why: A scientist makes a creature and rejects it; the Gothic classic about ambition and responsibility.

swamplandia.title: Swamplandia!
swamplandia.author: Karen Russell
swamplandia.why: A girl in a failing alligator park in the Everglades goes on a surreal journey; haunting and unsettling.

cold comfort farm.title: Cold Comfort Farm
cold comfort farm.author: Stella Gibbons
cold comfort farm.why: A sensible young woman tidies a gloomy farm of relatives; riotously funny and reread annually by fans.

deliverance.title: Deliverance
deliverance.author: James Dickey
deliverance.why: Four men on a canoe trip in Georgia face violence; short, intense and different from the film.

winds of war.title: The Winds of War
winds of war.author: Herman Wouk
winds of war.why: A naval officer's family faces the road to World War II; a long saga that readers call a favourite.

number of the beast.title: The Number of the Beast
number of the beast.author: Robert A. Heinlein
number of the beast.why: Comments do not discuss the book itself.

alice network.title: The Alice Network
alice network.author: Kate Quinn
alice network.why: Women spies in World War I and a search in 1947; a popular historical page-turner.

shock doctrine.title: The Shock Doctrine
shock doctrine.author: Naomi Klein
shock doctrine.why: Argues that crises are exploited to push free-market policy; a book some say they could not put down.

demon.title: The demon
demon.author: Hubert Selby, Jr.
demon.why: Comments discuss a different book, Varley's Demon, so the match is wrong.

emergence.title: Emergence
emergence.author: David R. Palmer
emergence.why: A young girl emerges from a fallout shelter after nuclear war; a childhood favourite.

foundryside.title: Foundryside
foundryside.author: Robert Jackson Bennett
foundryside.why: A thief in a city where objects can be programmed with magic; inventive and fast-paced.

destiny of the republic.title: The destiny of the republic
destiny of the republic.author: Candice Millard
destiny of the republic.why: The assassination of President Garfield told as a compelling narrative; a one-sitting read.

slapstick.title: Slapstick
slapstick.author: Kurt Vonnegut
slapstick.why: Vonnegut's weird tale of a giant-sized future; hilarious and sad together.

girl with all the gifts.title: The Girl with All the Gifts
girl with all the gifts.author: M. R. Carey
girl with all the gifts.why: A strange girl in a post-apocalyptic military base; tense, with a clever twist on the zombie story.

east.title: East
east.author: Edith Pattou
east.why: A girl travels with a white bear in a retelling of East of the Sun, West of the Moon; many reread yearly.

amber spyglass.title: The Amber Spyglass
amber spyglass.author: Philip Pullman
amber spyglass.why: Final book of His Dark Materials, resolving the multiverse story; a genuinely satisfying conclusion.

sea the sea.title: The Sea, the Sea
sea the sea.author: Iris Murdoch
sea the sea.why: A retired theatre director retires to the sea and becomes obsessed with a past love; readers rate it highly.

hollywood park.title: Hollywood Park
hollywood park.author: Mikel Jollett
hollywood park.why: A musician's childhood in a cult and in poverty; dark and painful but powerful.

before we were yours.title: Before We Were Yours
before we were yours.author: Lisa Wingate
before we were yours.why: Based on the real Tennessee Children's Home Society scandal; readers cried and were broken-hearted.

against a dark background.title: Against a Dark Background
against a dark background.author: Iain M. Banks
against a dark background.why: A noblewoman hunts relics in a dying star system; a dark, sprawling space adventure with fantasy flavour.

nineteen eighty four.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
nineteen eighty four.author: George Orwell
nineteen eighty four.why: Orwell's chilling vision of a totalitarian state and surveillance; its opening draws readers in.

trainspotting.title: Trainspotting
trainspotting.author: Irvine Welsh
trainspotting.why: Scottish heroin users in Edinburgh narrated in dialect; readers say it felt like a drug.

mysterious island.title: The Mysterious Island
mysterious island.author: Jules Verne
mysterious island.why: Castaways rebuild civilisation on a remote island in Verne's classic; loved since childhood.

friday afternoon club.title: The Friday Afternoon Club
friday afternoon club.author: Griffin Dunne
friday afternoon club.why: Actor and producer Dunne recalls growing up among Hollywood stars and family tragedy; readers call it extremely cool.

lullaby.title: Lullaby
lullaby.author: Chuck Palahniuk
lullaby.why: A reporter discovers a lullaby that kills; a strange, darkly funny Palahniuk novel.

red rabbit.title: Red Rabbit
red rabbit.author: Alex Grecian
red rabbit.why: An immersive Old West tale of pursuit; readers call it so good they cannot recommend it enough.

elsewhere.title: Elsewhere
elsewhere.author: Gabrielle Zevin
elsewhere.why: A teen girl wakes in the afterlife and learns to live backward in age; a gentle, lasting story about death.

blue sisters.title: Blue Sisters
blue sisters.author: Coco Mellors
blue sisters.why: Comments are mixed and focus on a bad audio narrator.

well of ascension.title: The Well of Ascension
well of ascension.author: Brandon Sanderson
well of ascension.why: Comments only mention reading it, no recommendation.

glass hotel.title: The Glass Hotel
glass hotel.author: Emily St. John Mandel
glass hotel.why: A Ponzi scheme and a remote hotel connect lives in Mandel's quietly eerie novel.

deadhouse gates.title: Deadhouse Gates (The Malazan Book of the Fallen, Book 2)
deadhouse gates.author: Steven Erikson
deadhouse gates.why: Second Malazan novel with a heartbreaking ending; readers want to walk the Chain of Dogs again.

london.title: London
london.author: Edward Rutherfurd
london.why: Follows several families through two thousand years of London's history.

new jim crow.title: The New Jim Crow
new jim crow.author: Michelle Alexander
new jim crow.why: Argues that mass incarceration works as a racial caste system; eye-opening and widely recommended.

katherine.title: Katherine
katherine.author: Anya Seton
katherine.why: Medieval romance about Katherine Swynford and John of Gaunt; top-tier historical fiction some reread yearly.
